national_news.title: PM Addresses Centenary Celebrations of Shri Ram College of Commerce in New Delhi
bullets: Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the centenary celebrations of Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC) in New Delhi.
He highlighted India's 7.8 percent quarterly economic growth rate amid global uncertainty, attributing it to a shift from policy paralysis to policy dynamism.
The event highlighted India's emergence as the world's third-largest startup ecosystem and the goal of achieving Viksit and Aatmanirbhar Bharat.

national_news.title: President Droupadi Murmu Confers National Teachers Awards
bullets: President Droupadi Murmu conferred the National Teachers Awards on the occasion of Teachers' Day in New Delhi.
A total of 48 selected school teachers from 27 States, seven Union Territories, and six Central Government organizations received the awards.
The President also presented National Awards to 21 faculty members and teachers from Higher Education Institutions and polytechnics.

national_news.title: PM Modi Interacts with 82 National Teachers' Day Award Winners
bullets: Prime Minister Narendra Modi interacted with 82 National Teachers' Award winners across school education, higher education, and skill development sectors.
He urged teachers to look beyond textbooks, emphasize experiential learning, and connect students with real-world practical skills under NEP guidance.
The PM raised concerns regarding excessive screen time among children and called for continuous awareness campaigns against drug abuse.

national_news.title: Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh Launches 'CSS Shield' Initiative
bullets: Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh launched the 'CSS Shield' initiative set up by the Central Secretariat Service (CSS) Forum in New Delhi.
The mechanism serves as a mutual financial support system aimed at providing a minimum assistance of Rs 15 lakh to the families of deceased CSS officers.
Since 2020, CSS officers have voluntarily contributed around Rs 1.30 crore to assist families of approximately 65 to 70 deceased colleagues.

national_news.title: UNGA Adopts Resolution to Standardize 'Equal Earth' Map Projection over Mercator Map
bullets: The UN General Assembly adopted the non-binding 'Correct the Map' resolution sponsored by Togo and supported by 164 nations, including India, France, and the UK.
The resolution advocates replacing the traditional 1569 Mercator map projection with the 2018 'Equal Earth projection' to accurately reflect the true relative sizes of continents.
The 16th-century Mercator map distorts landmasses near the poles, visually shrinking equatorial regions and depicting Africa as similar in size to Greenland despite being 14 times larger.

national_news.title: CSS Forum Launches 'CSS Shield' Mutual Financial Support Initiative for Families of Deceased Officers
bullets: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh launched the 'CSS Shield' initiative organized by the Central Secretariat Service (CSS) Forum in New Delhi.
The initiative establishes a structured mutual financial support mechanism aimed at providing at least Rs 15 lakh in financial assistance to the families of deceased CSS officers.
Since 2020, voluntary contributions by CSS officers have raised nearly Rs 1.30 crore to support 65–70 bereaved families of officers lost during and after the COVID-19 period.

national_news.title: EAM S. Jaishankar Visits Poland and Ukraine to Discuss Conflict Resolution
bullets: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar visited Poland and Ukraine, reiterating India's stance that dialogue and diplomacy should end the ongoing conflict.
Discussions with Polish leaders included reviewing the Joint Action Plan 2024-28 focusing on trade, defence, and global challenges like supply chain resilience.
India emphasized its willingness to play a constructive role in humanitarian assistance and peace efforts between Russia and Ukraine.

national_news.title: UN General Assembly Adopts Resolution to Correct African Continent Size on Maps
bullets: The UN General Assembly voted to adopt the 'Correct the Map' resolution, sponsored by Togo and backed by the African Union, replacing the traditional Mercator map.
The traditional 16th-century Mercator map distorts landmasses, showing Africa similar in size to Greenland despite being 14 times larger.
The non-binding resolution encourages institutions to adopt representations like the Equal Earth projection for accurate geographical proportions.

national_news.title: MEA Highlights Assistance to Nepal and Progress on Greater Malé Connectivity Project
bullets: The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) confirmed the rescue of 166 Indian nationals in flood-hit Nepal, announcing plans to dispatch Bailey bridges and forensic kits as relief support.
MEA reported that the first segment of the India-assisted Greater Malé Connectivity Project in the Maldives, which connects capital Malé with three adjacent islands, has been completed.
During EAM Dr. S. Jaishankar's visit to Ukraine, India reaffirmed its stance emphasizing dialogue and diplomacy to resolve the ongoing conflict.

national_news.title: Inaugural Drass District Festival 2026 Focuses on Eco-Tourism and Bear Conservation
bullets: The first-ever two-day Drass District Festival 2026 was inaugurated in the newly established district of Drass in Ladakh to promote sustainable tourism and cultural heritage.
A guided Nature Trail was conducted to raise awareness about the fragile ecosystem of Drass and Mushkoh valleys, focusing on conserving the endangered Himalayan Brown Bear.
The event showcased traditional Horse Polo, local handicrafts, and cultural performances to establish Drass as an eco- and adventure-tourism hub.

bihar_news.title: Bihar to Establish 700 Model Schools, Teacher Training Varsity, and AI Ecosystem
bullets: The Bihar government announced plans to set up ~700 Saraswati Vidya Niketan Model Schools equipped with live online guidance for NEET and JEE exam preparation.
A dedicated Teacher Training University will be established, alongside an MoU signed with Google to train over 7 lakh state teachers in AI technologies.

Key education reforms include target timelines for matric (7 days) and polytechnic results (24 hours), a High Court judge-led exam reform committee, and land acquisition completion for Vikramshila University.

bihar_news.title: Bihar Mandates Prior Consent for CBI Probes Against State Public Servants
bullets: The Home Department of Bihar issued a notification making state government consent mandatory for the CBI to investigate offences involving Bihar public servants and state-controlled entities.
The notification accords general consent for CBI investigations against Central Government employees, Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs), and central private entities in Bihar.
The CBI derives its powers from Section 6 of the Delhi Special Police Establishment (DSPE) Act, 1946, which requires state consent for exercising jurisdiction within state borders.

bihar_news.title: Bihar Mandates Pre-Approval for CBI Investigations Involving State Officials
bullets: The Bihar government has restricted general consent for the Central Bureau of Investigation, mandating case-by-case prior permission to probe state officials.
Issued under Section 6 of the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946, the notification ensures localized state oversight on investigative proposals.
Central Government employees, Central PSUs, and central agency-controlled individuals remain covered under general consent within the state.

bihar_news.title: RVNL Bags ₹903 Crore Infrastructure Order for Buxar Thermal Power Project
bullets: Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL) received a Letter of Award worth ₹903.01 crore from SJVN Thermal Private Limited for railway siding works in Bihar.
The contract involves constructing a permanent railway siding and aerial track connection to Chausa and Pawani Kamarpur under Phase-III of the 1,320 MW Buxar Thermal Power Project (BTPP).
The domestic infrastructure project has an execution timeline of 36 months.
